title: Come, Thou Soul-transforming Spirit
description: Come, Thou Soul-transforming Spirit in Tonic Solfa to ST. AUSTIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: William Jay wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 82 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Prayer for a Blessing”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked 8.7.8.7.4.7, to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AUSTIN; any other 8.7.8.7.4.7 tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, thou soul trans-form-ing Spir-it, Bless the sow-er and the seed; Let each heart thy grace in-her-it; Raise the weak, the hun-gry feed; From the gos-pel Now sup-ply thy peo-ple's need.

lines: Bless the sower and the seed;
Let each heart thy grace inherit;
Raise the weak, the hungry feed;
O, may all enjoy the blessing
Which thy word's designed to give,
Let us all, thy love possessing,
To thy praise and glory live.

licence: Public domain: William Jay died in 1853.
credits: Words by William Jay (1769–1853), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AUSTIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
